before: If your promises still mean something to your little one, maybe because you've kept a few small ones, a quiet vow can help too. You can say it with or without picturing the two of you playing on a swing set:
after: (Not written yet. The next paragraph: say the "I love you" part only if it's honest; if it isn't yet, use the goodwill wish from "A Smaller Doorway: Goodwill" or a promise not to be cruel to them. Don't say any of that here.)
brief:
- This paragraph is the vow itself: what the reader says to their little one, as one quote in quotation marks. Every line of the guide's vow stays, said the way a person would actually say it out loud (contractions, plain words):
  - "I know you are in there. I love you."
  - "You do not have to love me back or trust me yet." (Love Doesn't Have to Wait for Trust already has "You don't have to love me back" in the answer to "Big fuckity whoopty doo". The vow says it again on purpose, now as a promise.)
  - what you can't promise: that nothing painful will happen, that you'll always know what to do, or that you'll never react badly
  - what you can promise: to tell them the truth, listen when they're angry, make your life together safer where you can, take the next protective step you can see, and come back to repair when you fail
  - "You do not have to believe these words. Watch what I do."
- Don't add promises, reasons or feelings, and don't explain the vow. Nothing before or after the quote: the paragraph before leads into it with a colon, and the next paragraph is about the "I love you".
- No asterisk or footnote mark after "I love you".
voice: in the first person, as the reader speaking to their little one, all inside quotation marks
guide_passage: “I know you are in there. I love you.* You do not have to love me back or trust me yet. I cannot promise that nothing painful will happen, that I will always know what to do, or that I will never react badly. I can promise to tell you the truth, listen when you are angry, make our life safer where I can, take the next protective step I can see, and come back to repair when I fail. You do not have to believe these words. Watch what I do.”
next: Use “I love you” only when it is honest. Otherwise, use a sincere wish for wellbeing or a commitment to non-cruelty without pretending they feel the same.
